Future crypto reuse material is retained under a 128 MiB / 2048-file bound with hashes and manifest; it contains public source/build inputs and requires separate future admission.

New schema declares loopback normal-send-cap-1024 scope, forced partial sends false, receiver segmentation uncontrolled and general TCP segmentation unaccepted. Full send calls do not guarantee a single server receive.

All four fresh baseline cases retain strict original probe result admission. Existing seven-byte probe separately records either exact known reset or narrowly admitted success; neither grants general TCP fragmentation acceptance.
No prior login, service cleanup or failed fragmentation acceptance is inherited. Whole-run pass still requires baseline cases, historical observation, service/lifetime checks and unchanged sources.

New process diagnostics query only numeric owned SQL PID, process name/start ticks and bounded unique Job-member PIDs; they record before/after cleanup state without killing or mutating an extra process.

Process/listener, firewall, SQL schema/instance and private-file cleanup requirements remain unchanged. Diagnostic failure revokes baseline aggregate acceptance; previous SQL DROP failure remains a failure.
Original receive-offset source oracle is a workflow precondition and retains known failure evidence. No accepted APK, Android renderer or production server binary is rebuilt or patched.
